channel.title: Mapping Forward
channel.description: Daily synthesis of articles on cartography, mapping, geospatial data, and geographic intelligence

item.title: TomTom and citiEU Strengthen Ties to Deliver Advanced Traffic Monitoring and Location Analytics
item.description: TomTom announced an expanded partnership with citiEU to deliver advanced location analytics, traffic intelligence, and mobility solutions across Europe and the Middle East, leveraging TomTom's full product portfolio including Traffic Analytics. — Key takeaways: citiEU will leverage TomTom's location intelligence to support advanced location analytics, traffic intelligence, and mobility solutions ; The expanded agreement covers clients in Europe and the Middle East ; citiEU will use a broad portfolio of TomTom products including Traffic Analytics, traffic volumes, and routing data ; The partnership was announced September 10, 2026 from Amsterdam ; TomTom positions itself as "the specialist in mapping and location technology" ; Multiple financial and trade outlets covered the announcement (Yahoo Finance, Zonebourse, TradingView, Barchart)

item.title: Xpeng Integrates Google Maps Into Its Embedded Navigation
item.description: Chinese automaker Xpeng has integrated Google Maps cartographic data and navigation capabilities directly into its embedded vehicle navigation system — not as an app, but as a native integration of Google's mapping data. — Key takeaways: Google Maps data arrives natively in Xpeng vehicles, not as a standalone application ; Xpeng integrates Google's cartographic data and navigational APIs for the first time ; This makes Xpeng the first Chinese automaker to natively integrate Google Maps data ; The integration provides real-time cartographic data and navigation features ; Previous coverage noted Xpeng's integration of Google Maps Auto SDK in August 2026

item.title: Correcting the Map, as We Must, and Yet Still
item.description: A legal scholar analyzes the UN's "Correct the Map" resolution (A/RES/80/297), arguing that correcting cartographic representation is a matter of cognitive justice — recognizing and contesting inherited colonial ways of seeing the world. — Key takeaways: 164 UN Member States adopted resolution A/RES/80/297, with only one voting against ; The resolution was led by Togo on behalf of the African Group, building on an African Union campaign ; The Equal Earth projection was developed in 2018 by researchers at Esri, US National Park Service, and Monash University ; Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey framed the issue as "cognitive justice" — access to geographical knowledge, dignity, and historical memory ; The Mercator projection "midwifed a particular global socio-economic and political order" centered on Europe ; The author argues that no perfectly neutral map exists; every projection involves choices about what to preserve

item.title: Will the UN Decision Change Our World Maps?
item.description: The UN General Assembly adopted a resolution with 164 votes in favor and one against, calling for world maps to use representations that more faithfully reflect the relative size of continents — favoring the Equal Earth projection over the colonial-era Mercator projection. — Key takeaways: The resolution was passed with 164 votes for and 1 against, presented by a coalition of African countries led by Togo ; The Equal Earth projection, developed in 2018, preserves proportional area while accepting distortions elsewhere ; Greenland appears similar in size to Africa on Mercator maps, but Africa is actually 14 times larger ; Brazil appears the same size as Alaska on Mercator but is in reality five times larger ; UQAM geography professor Rodolphe Gonzalès frames this as a "symbolic injustice, a geometric injustice between North and South" ; Google Maps and other navigators predominantly use Mercator because it enables smooth zoom

item.title: California Keeps Widening Roads. Traffic Keeps Getting Worse.
item.description: California ranks as the third most congested state in the US according to the TomTom Traffic Index, and billions spent on road widening show no clear evidence of reducing traffic — illustrating the phenomenon of induced demand. — Key takeaways: California was the 3rd most congested state in the US in the 2025 TomTom Traffic Index ; Los Angeles ranked 25th worldwide for worst average congestion, with 59.8% time lost to traffic ; LA drivers lose 83 hours during rush hour per year; San Francisco has the 6th worst congestion in North America ; San Francisco has the lowest average speed (12.6 mph) and lowest average distance in 15 minutes (4.5 miles) in the US ; The American Society of Civil Engineers gave California roadways a "D" grade ; Transport for America reports that "expanding highways to improve traffic flow can actually increase congestion by encouraging people to drive more" ; Nearly one-third of California's roads are in poor condition

item.title: Geo Week Announces Strategic Partnerships for 2027 Event
item.description: Geo Week 2027 has announced its strategic partnerships including event partners ASPRS and Reality Capture Network, industry partners including GISCI, ISPRS, and NSPS, and 185+ supporting partner organizations spanning six continents. — Key takeaways: Geo Week 2027 will take place February 23-25, 2027, in Salt Lake City, Utah ; Event Partners: ASPRS (American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing) and Reality Capture Network (RCN) ; Industry Partners include GISCI, ISPRS, MAPPS, NSPS, OGC, USGIF, USIBD, and WGIC ; New partnerships with Utah-based organizations UGIC and SLUG reflect local community engagement ; Women in GIS will participate, strengthening diversity initiatives ; 185+ supporting partner organizations span six continents ; Registration is open with Super Saver pricing

item.title: Google Maps Begins Blurring South Korean Military Sites and the DMZ
item.description: Google Maps has begun blurring satellite imagery of military sites in South Korea and the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), complying with South Korean security regulations regarding the publication of sensitive military installations. — Key takeaways: Google Maps has started blurring satellite imagery of South Korean military sites ; The DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) imagery is also being blurred ; This follows South Korean security regulations regarding sensitive military installations ; The blurring affects satellite view imagery visible to all Google Maps users ; South Korea has long requested satellite platforms to obscure military installations

item.title: Japan Seeks Change to New UN World Map Over Russia 'Misconception'
item.description: Japan has formally requested changes to the new UN "true-scale" world map, arguing that it depicts the disputed Kuril Islands as ruled by Moscow — a depiction Tokyo considers a "misconception" of its territorial sovereignty. — Key takeaways: The new 'true-scale' map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa ; Japan objects to the map showing the disputed Kuril Islands as Russian territory ; The Kuril Islands have been disputed between Japan and Russia since WWII ; Japan's objection highlights how map representations carry political and territorial implications beyond mere cartographic accuracy ; The UN adopted the Equal Earth-type map with 164 votes for and 1 against

item.title: Esri and Saint Louis University to Advance Geospatial Research and Innovation
item.description: Esri has entered into an official partnership with Saint Louis University's Geospatial Institute (GeoSLU) to advance GIS research addressing global challenges including climate change, food security, and economic stability, with both organizations affiliated with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. — Key takeaways: Saint Louis University recently founded the Geospatial Institute (GeoSLU) ; Both SLU and Esri are affiliated with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) ; Esri has collaborated with NGA for 30 years; SLU signed a CRADA with NGA last year ; Projects include an "Ideathon" called "Saving the Herd with AI" using ArcGIS Online to counter wildlife trafficking ; Jack Dangermond, Esri founder, will participate at Geo-Resolution, a geospatial collaboration event ; Research focus areas include climate change, access to food and clean water, and economic stability

item.title: Field Evaluation of Photogrammetric SLAM for Infrastructure Asset Mapping
item.description: A field evaluation at BCIT compares Looq AI's handheld photogrammetric mapping platform against Total Station and GNSS RTK survey methods for infrastructure asset mapping, finding that the system can support precision mapping when used with rigorous survey control protocols. — Key takeaways: Looq AI's Platform combines imagery, GNSS, and inertial sensing to produce georeferenced 3D data ; Evaluation conducted on a 150m x 50m outdoor plaza at BCIT Burnaby campus with ~45-47 manhole/utility features ; Reference framework established via Leica TS13 Robotic Total Station with closed traverse tied to BCIT geodetic network ; Leica GS06 GNSS RTK receiver provided comparison via Leica SmartNet CORS network ; In the no-control test, the Looq dataset exceeded the 50mm tolerance for GIS asset management ; With external ground control alignment, accuracy improved significantly ; Wet surface conditions from post-rain capture did not significantly affect geometry or detection accuracy

item.title: AI Maps Global Methane Emissions from Space with NASA's EMIT Instrument
item.description: Google and NASA JPL introduced MAPL-EMIT, an AI model that detects 50% more methane plumes than human experts by analyzing satellite imagery, identifying over 23,000 additional plumes globally. — Key takeaways: MAPL-EMIT is a deep learning model from Google Research and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, published in PNAS ; Trained on 3.6 million physics-simulated methane plumes, it detects 50% more plumes than human experts ; The model identified over 23,000 additional plumes globally, including 24 of the 25 world's largest-emitting landfills ; Methane has 30 times the warming potential of CO2 over a 100-year timeframe ; Google released the global plume database on Earth Engine, with open-source models on Kaggle and GitHub

item.title: Extending the TomTom Maps and Navigation SDK Android Example App with Claude Code
item.description: TomTom demonstrates how Claude Code can extend its Android Maps and Navigation SDK example app by building a Route Instructions Panel feature, documenting pitfalls in a reusable skill file. — Key takeaways: TomTom used Anthropic's Claude Code AI agent to build a Route Instructions Panel — a draggable bottom sheet listing every maneuver on a planned route — on top of their Android SDK example app ; The agent mapped nine routing instruction subtypes (departures, turns, forks, merges, roundabouts, highway exits, tollgates, arrivals) to icons and natural-language phrases ; Key challenges included type-shape surprises in the SDK (e.g., `Road.name` returning `TextWithPhonetics?` not `String?`), packages in unexpected locations, and experimental Compose APIs that compile but crash at runtime ; The experiment is fully reproducible: prompt, CLAUDE.md, and skill file are published in a GitHub repo, pinned to exact app commit and SDK version ; The Superpowers plugin by Jesse Vincent was used to add workflow skills on top of Claude Code

item.title: In Maps and Charts: Russian and Ukrainian Attacks on Civilian Targets
item.description: Al Jazeera's data visualization maps how both sides in the Russia-Ukraine war have increasingly targeted civilian infrastructure, with drone attacks more than doubling and interception rates falling. — Key takeaways: Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure rose from 5% of all attacks in 2022 to 13% by August 2026 (7,170 incidents), per ACLED data ; Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure rose from 10% in 2022 to 27% by August 2026 (3,560 incidents) ; Donetsk (3,652 attacks) and Belgorod (9,549 attacks) are the most targeted regions on each side ; Drones now dominate the war, replacing artillery as the primary attack method, with Ukraine planning 1,000 drone launches per day ; Missile interception rates fell from 24% in 2025 to 10.2% in 2026 due to dwindling Patriot and IRIS-T interceptor supplies

item.title: Mapping the Global Health Landscape: Analysis of Fourteen International Organizations
item.description: KFF published a descriptive mapping of 14 key global health institutions to inform discussions about duplication, synergies, and architectural reform in the global health ecosystem. — Key takeaways: KFF mapped 14 key global health and related international institutions, focusing on their work in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) ; The mapping examines mandates, governance models, financing structures, and operational approaches across organizations ; Multiple reform efforts are underway: the Lusaka Agenda, the Accra Reset, and WHO's Joint Process on Reform of the Global Health Architecture ; The mapping is descriptive, not evaluative — it does not assess organizational performance or effectiveness ; The report is intended to inform discussions about synergies, coordination, duplication, and comparative advantage across entities

item.title: Esri India Launches Free Digital Atlas Program to Make School Geography Genuinely Interesting
item.description: Esri India launched a free Digital Atlas Program built on ArcGIS Online, giving schoolteachers interactive mapping tools to transform geography from memorization to real-world investigation. — Key takeaways: Esri India launched the Digital Atlas Program, offering interactive digital mapping tools and curriculum-relevant content free to schools across India ; Built on ArcGIS Online, the program provides interactive tools to explore layers of real-world data: population patterns, weather, land use, and more ; The initiative shifts students from asking "where is it" to "why is it there," examining real-world events like flooding through data ; GIS in classrooms has been linked to measurable gains in analytical skills and stronger STEM performance ; The program targets spatial and geographic literacy — skills that underpin urban planning, disaster management, and climate science

item.title: Google Maps Loses Speedometer and Speed Limits on Android Auto Just Weeks After Launch
item.description: A bug on Android Auto causes Google Maps' newly launched speedometer and speed limit display to disappear, along with traffic lights and stop signs, while everything works fine on Apple CarPlay. — Key takeaways: Google Maps' real-time speedometer, deployed on Android Auto in July 2026, has disappeared for many users due to a display bug ; The bug also removes speed limit indicators, and in some cases traffic lights, stop signs, and traffic lines ; Apple CarPlay remains unaffected — the speedometer and all indicators continue working normally ; Some users recovered the feature by leaving the Google Maps and Android Auto beta channels and reinstalling stable versions, but this workaround is inconsistent ; Google has not issued an official fix or statement; Waze is also experiencing display glitches

item.title: Satellite Navigators Concentrate Traffic on Few Roads, Reducing Environmental Benefits
item.description: A study published in Nature Communications shows that when adoption of navigation apps like Google Maps and TomTom exceeds 60–80%, traffic concentrates on few roads and environmental benefits disappear or reverse. — Key takeaways: Research by CNR-Isti, University of Pisa, and Scuola Normale Superiore simulated traffic in Florence, Milan, and Rome using GPS data cross-referenced with Google Maps, TomTom, Bing Maps, and Mapbox routing ; Route diversity decreases up to 14% at full adoption, pushing vehicles toward major arteries and highways ; With light traffic, navigators reduce CO2 emissions; with heavy traffic, benefits only hold below 60–80% adoption ; Beyond that threshold, benefits "attenuate, vanish, or even reverse" — in some Rome scenarios, emissions actually increased ; The study highlights how individual-level optimization algorithms can produce collectively harmful outcomes at scale

item.title: TomTom's New Route Runs Through AI: Discovery Event Reveals Strategic Pivot
item.description: At its TomTom Discovery Event in Amsterdam, the company revealed a fundamental strategic repositioning: maps are no longer primarily for guiding people, but for navigating AI and machines, with Orbis serving as a spatial knowledge layer for autonomous driving and enterprise AI agents. — Key takeaways: TomTom is shifting from 40 years of helping humans understand the physical world to helping intelligent systems and AI understand and move within it ; CEO Mike Schoofs aims to provide the critical safety map layer for more than half of all new European cars by 2030 ; The company has transitioned from hardware (navigation devices with ~40% margins) to pure software (gross margins heading toward 90%) ; Orbis Maps serves as "ground truth" — a uniform, verified reference reality combining OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps, TomTom's own data, and vehicle sensor data ; The platform uses more than 5 billion data points to continuously enrich and verify the map, with 2.8 trillion kilometres of worldwide distance data stored ; TomTom has made Orbis APIs and an MCP server available for AI agents to access spatial intelligence ; Location intelligence is identified as a double-digit growth market, with 70-80% of enterprise data containing a spatial component

item.title: Iceland Summons US Ambassador After Trump Posts Map Showing Iceland as US Territory
item.description: Iceland has summoned the US ambassador after President Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the entire North American continent — including Iceland — covered by the American flag, escalating a series of cartographic provocations that now intersect with Google Maps' renaming of Lake Ontario to "Lake America." — Key takeaways: Iceland's Foreign Minister Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir summoned US Ambassador Billy Long to signal that the image was "totally inappropriate" ; Trump posted the map on Truth Social showing the US, Central America, Canada, Greenland, and Iceland covered by the American flag, with no caption ; The incident follows Trump's persistent territorial ambitions regarding Greenland, a Danish autonomous territory whose coast is less than 300 km from Iceland ; Trump previously confused Greenland with Iceland in January 2026 ; Iceland has been independent since 1944, has no army, and relies on NATO and a 1951 bilateral defense agreement with the US for security ; Icelandic voters rejected EU accession negotiations in an August 29 referendum, maintaining their balance of European economic integration and Atlantic defense posture ; The map incident coincides with Google Maps displaying "Lake America" instead of Lake Ontario within the United States

item.title: This Little-Known Google Maps Setting Saves Your Battery and Mobile Data
item.description: Google Maps' offline maps feature can save both battery and mobile data, but a hidden default setting silently updates downloaded maps over cellular data without user confirmation — here's how to fix it. — Key takeaways: GPS navigation is one of the most battery-intensive tasks on a smartphone, simultaneously using GPS, screen, CPU, and mobile data ; Google Maps' offline maps feature allows pre-downloading detailed maps to navigate without a network connection ; Once downloaded, the app no longer needs to constantly request mobile data to display streets and points of interest ; A hidden default setting automatically updates offline maps over both Wi-Fi and cellular data without asking for confirmation ; The update process runs in the background with no notification or visible indication ; Disabling "Automatically update offline maps" and "Automatically download recommended maps" prevents unwanted data consumption ; Restricting offline map updates to Wi-Fi only further protects mobile data allowances

item.title: Fairmont State's Frank LaFone Honored with Geospatial Lifetime Achievement Award
item.description: Dr. Frank LaFone, geography faculty member at Fairmont State University, has received the West Virginia Association of Geospatial Professionals Lifetime Achievement Award for over two decades of contributions to GIS and geospatial technology across the state. — Key takeaways: Dr. Frank LaFone honored with the WVAGP Lifetime Achievement Award for career-long contributions to GIS in West Virginia ; He was a founding member and key architect of the West Virginia Association of Geospatial Professionals (WVAGP) ; LaFone earned his GISP certification early in the program's history and served multiple terms on the WVAGP Board, including as president and vice president ; He co-founded VerySpatial, one of the longest-running geography and geospatial podcasts, contributing to professional education nationally and internationally ; The award was presented at WV GEOCON, West Virginia's annual geospatial conference ; As a faculty member at Fairmont State University, LaFone continues to connect students with geospatial technology opportunities to address community needs

item.title: TomTom Expands EV Charger Data Past 2 Million Points
item.description: TomTom now covers more than two million EV charging points globally and plans to ship an AI-based battery range prediction model by the end of 2026, as the company reports delivering on its two-year EV roadmap with overhauled POI data, availability profiles, and live pricing. — Key takeaways: TomTom's EV charging data now covers over 2 million charging points globally ; Availability profiles use six weeks of rolling usage data to predict charger busyness at expected arrival time ; A "super aggregator" model works with regional data partners rather than connecting to every charge point operator individually ; Driver demand has shifted from finding a charger to choosing one based on price, amenities, security, and weather protection ; An AI-based range prediction API is on track for release by end of 2026, using learning models trained on actual usage data ; The EV product group has been reorganized as Destination and Waypoint Management, expanding to cover POI search, fuel prices, parking, and in-car transactions ; Vehicle-to-grid and vehicle-to-load functions are flagged as growing in importance, but driver experience must be reliable

item.title: The Next Chapter in Electric Driving Isn't About EVs
item.description: TomTom reviews its two-year EV roadmap, revealing that EV charging data now covers over 2 million points globally, with AI-based range prediction and background intelligence features planned by year-end as the company shifts focus from simply finding chargers to helping drivers choose the right one. — Key takeaways: EVs now account for close to 30% of new car sales across Europe on average, with battery EVs at 20%; Norway leads at over 97% ; TomTom has overhauled its EV charging POI data, added availability profiles, live pricing, and unified its search and routing stack for EV-specific navigation ; The company uses a "super aggregator" model, working with regional data partners rather than connecting to every charge point operator individually ; Driver demand has shifted from finding a charger to choosing one based on price, amenities, security, and covered parking ; An AI-based range prediction API is on track for release by end of 2026, moving from multi-variate equations to learning models trained on actual usage data ; The EV team has been reorganized as "Destination and Waypoint Management," expanding scope to POI search, fuel prices, parking, and in-car transactions

item.title: Five Colombian Cities Rank Among World's Most Congested According to TomTom Traffic Index
item.description: The TomTom Traffic Index 2025 reveals that four Colombian cities — Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, and Barranquilla — rank among the 20 most congested in the world, with Bogotá leading at 69.6% congestion, underscoring a national challenge in urban mobility planning. — Key takeaways: Bogotá recorded the highest congestion level among Colombian cities at 69.6%, meaning travel times were on average 69.6% longer than free-flow conditions ; Medellín followed at 66.9%, Cali at 65.6%, Barranquilla at 62.8%, and Cartagena at 57.7% ; Four Colombian cities placed among the 20 most congested cities globally in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025 ; All five major Colombian cities exceeded 57% congestion, well above the global average ; Graphisoft identifies five keys for modernizing road infrastructure: integrate information from the start, simulate before building, detect errors early, plan for future growth, and strengthen digital talent ; The use of open standards like IFC is recommended to ensure information accessibility across all project stakeholders

item.title: Wildfire Map Spotlight: Konitsa Fire, Greece
item.description: A major wildfire in Greece's Konitsa region is burning in rugged mountain terrain near Vikos-Aoos National Park, with 170 firefighters deployed and emergency alerts issued to residents amid heavy smoke and difficult access conditions. — Key takeaways: The Konitsa wildfire began August 31, 2026 and intensified through September 7 in the Trapezitsa area near Konitsa, Epirus, northwestern Greece ; About 170 firefighters, 45 vehicles, 20 support vehicles, aircraft, helicopters, and drone teams are involved in suppression efforts ; A 112 emergency alert was sent to Konitsa residents urging alertness due to the wildfire and heavy smoke ; The fire threatens Vikos-Aoos National Park, the Aoos Gorge, and the Tymfi mountain area ; Steep terrain, dense vegetation, and strong flare-ups continue to complicate firefighting operations ; The trail toward Stomio Monastery was preventively closed due to fire and dense smoke

item.title: Movie Scene Map: A Free Interactive Map of 16,000 Film and Series Locations Worldwide
item.description: Movie Scene Map is a free interactive map listing nearly 16,000 real filming locations across 166 countries, letting users discover which films and series were shot near their home, with a particularly rich collection of Parisian locations. — Key takeaways: Movie Scene Map catalogs nearly 16,000 real filming locations across 166 countries ; The platform covers over 10,000 films and series, plus video games, anime, and manga locations ; Paris is among the most represented cities, with locations from Mission: Impossible – Fallout, Emily in Paris, and other productions ; France has nearly 1,000 listed filming locations including châteaux, beaches, villages, stations, and streets ; Users can search by location by zooming on the map, or by film title to find all shooting locations ; The map includes fictional locations from anime and manga rather than physical filming sites

item.title: African Union Welcomes UN Adoption of "Correct the Map" Resolution
item.description: The Chairperson of the African Union Commission welcomed the UN's adoption of the "Correct the Map" resolution, praising Togo's leadership in mobilizing African states to correct the Mercator projection's visual shrinking of Africa's true size. — Key takeaways: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf welcomed the UN adoption of the "Correct the Map" resolution ; He praised Togo's leadership and President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé for championing the initiative on behalf of Africa ; The AU Commission noted the Mercator projection gives a "considerably reduced visual representation of the real size of the African continent" ; The AU encourages international institutions, education systems, publishers, and digital actors to progressively adopt more faithful cartographic representations ; Togo's diplomacy hailed the adoption as "a victory for accuracy" and pledged to focus on concrete implementation ; The resolution passed with 164 votes in favor on September 4, 2026

item.title: Google Maps: Disable These Settings to Protect Your Privacy and Battery
item.description: Clubic details three key Google Maps settings to disable for better privacy and battery life: turning off Timeline location history, enabling incognito navigation mode, and restricting offline map auto-updates to Wi-Fi only. — Key takeaways: Google Maps' Timeline feature records every trip, stop, and route by default, storing data on the device ; Users can disable Timeline or set auto-deletion after 3 months instead of permanent recording ; Incognito mode suspends location history recording, search tracking, and personalized recommendations ; Offline maps auto-update by default over both Wi-Fi and cellular data, draining battery and consuming mobile data ; Users can restrict offline map downloads to Wi-Fi only and disable auto-updates in Settings ; All three settings are accessible through the profile photo menu in Google Maps

item.title: INMO GO3 AI Glasses Win IFA Innovation Award with HERE Maps Navigation
item.description: The INMO GO3 lightweight AI glasses won the IFA Innovation Award, integrating HERE Maps for hands-free pedestrian and cycling navigation with step-by-step directions displayed directly in the glasses. — Key takeaways: INMO GO3 AI glasses won the IFA Innovation Award for innovations in the wearable technology domain ; The GO3 integrate HERE Maps for pedestrian and cycling navigation in hands-free mode ; Navigation directions are displayed step-by-step directly in the glasses' display ; HERE Maps provides the mapping and routing backbone for the glasses' navigation features ; The glasses are positioned as lightweight AI eyewear designed for everyday use ; The award was announced at IFA, one of the world's leading consumer electronics trade shows

item.title: Could the World Map Change? What the UN's New Move Means for India
item.description: The UN General Assembly's "Correct the Map" resolution passed 164-1 with six abstentions, encouraging equal-area projections that show Africa's true size, but India's support comes with a caveat about Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh representation. — Key takeaways: The UN General Assembly adopted the "Correct the Map" resolution on September 4, 2026, with 164 votes in favor, 1 against (United States), and 6 abstentions ; The resolution was introduced by Togo on behalf of African countries and encourages wider use of equal-area map projections ; The Equal Earth projection (2018) preserves relative landmass sizes: Africa appears larger, Europe and North America smaller, India slightly larger ; The resolution does not ban the Mercator projection or legally require countries to use Equal Earth ; India voted in favor but clarified it supports equal-area mapping broadly, not one specific projection ; India demanded any UN-backed map accurately depict Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh per India's official map

item.title: Map: Top People From Each Bay Area City, According to Wikipedia Views
item.description: The San Francisco Chronicle built an interactive map showing the most-viewed Wikipedia person from every Bay Area city, using Wikimedia API pageview data spanning August 2021 to August 2026 to reveal the hometown heroes of each locality. — Key takeaways: The Chronicle mapped the most-viewed Wikipedia person from every Bay Area city and town ; Data was collected using the Wikidata Query Service to retrieve Bay Area cities and match them to Wikipedia "people from" pages ; Pageview data was gathered via the Wikimedia API from August 27, 2021 to August 27, 2026 ; ChatGPT was used to add links for about two dozen towns whose lists were not on Wikipedia's California page ; The map is interactive, allowing users to click and drag to explore and see who tops each location ; The project combines geographic data with cultural data to create a data journalism visualization

item.title: Bucharest Traffic Nightmare Unchanged: 10 Kilometers in Over 45 Minutes at Rush Hour
item.description: Bucharest ranks 20th globally in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025, with drivers losing nearly 171 hours per year in traffic — a 10km trip taking over 45 minutes at evening rush hour, and conditions worsening compared to 2024. — Key takeaways: Bucharest ranks 20th worldwide in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025 for most congested cities ; A 10-kilometer trip takes over 32 minutes on average, exceeding 45 minutes during evening rush hour ; Average speed during congested periods drops to approximately 14 km/h ; Drivers lose nearly 171 hours per year in traffic, equivalent to over 7 days ; October 7, 2025 was the most congested day, with congestion reaching 106% and 176% at 5 PM ; Travel times for 10km trips increased by 1 minute 11 seconds compared to 2024, while average rush hour speed decreased by 1 km/h

item.title: UN General Assembly Votes to Promote Equal Earth Projection for More Accurate World Maps
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to promote equal-area map projections like Equal Earth, encouraging governments, schools, and tech companies to represent continents at their true relative sizes rather than the distorted Mercator view used since the 16th century. — Key takeaways: The UN General Assembly voted on September 4, 2026, with 164 in favor, 1 against, and 6 abstentions to promote equal-area world map projections ; The resolution was sponsored by Togo and encourages governments, educational institutions, international organizations, and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections ; The 2018 Equal Earth projection is identified as an example of a map that accurately represents continental scale ; The resolution does not formally replace or prohibit the Mercator projection, which has been used since the 16th century ; It calls for education about the limitations of representing Earth's curved surface on a two-dimensional map ; The resolution is non-binding but could influence cartographic standards in education and digital mapping

item.title: New UN Map Depicts Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin as Territories Caught Between Indian and Chinese Lines
item.description: A new UN world map published following the "Correct the Map" resolution depicts Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin as territories between Indian and Chinese claim lines, prompting India's MEA to reiterate that any inaccurate depiction of its sovereign territory is unacceptable. — Key takeaways: The UN map published July 1, 2026 shows Arunachal Pradesh's southern border with Assam as the "Chinese Line" and its northern border with Tibet as the "Indian Line" ; Aksai Chin's eastern borders are labeled "Indian Line" while a "Chinese line" demarcates Ladakh from Aksai Chin ; India claims Aksai Chin as part of Ladakh, but the map shows separate Indian and Chinese claim lines without explanatory notes ; The map depicts Jammu and Kashmir with a dotted Line of Control, clarified as an India-Pakistan agreement with final status not yet agreed ; India's MEA reiterated that the vote supported the principle of equal-area representation, not endorsement of any specific map or boundary depiction ; The map appears to favor India on the Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura border dispute with Nepal, reflecting Indian control

item.title: Volcanic Eruption Map Spotlight: Anak Krakatau, Indonesia
item.description: Anak Krakatau volcano in Indonesia's Sunda Strait erupted on September 4, 2026, sending ash plumes to 50,000 feet, disrupting 300+ flights, and prompting evacuation zones and air quality monitoring via interactive maps. — Key takeaways: Anak Krakatau began erupting on September 4, 2026, producing lava fountains and ash plumes reaching approximately 50,000 feet ; The volcano is at Alert Level III (second-highest on Indonesia's four-level scale) ; Over 300 flights were affected, with airports in Jakarta, Bandung, and Lampung disrupted ; Authorities established a 3-kilometer exclusion zone around the active crater ; Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency plans cloud seeding to encourage rainfall that may help remove ash from affected areas

item.title: New Maps Show How Israel Has Thwarted Hopes for a Palestinian State
item.description: Ten years after maps of Israeli settlements shocked President Obama, updated 2026 maps show that settlement expansion has confined Palestinians to just 8% of the land, rendering the two-state solution virtually impossible. — Key takeaways: Over 500,000 Jewish settlers now live among 3 million Palestinians in the West Bank ; Since 2023, Israel approved 104 new settlements, up from just 3 during the entire Obama Administration ; Settler attacks documented by the UN surged from 107 in 2016 to over 5,300 since 2023 — more than 4 per day ; Palestinians now control approximately 8% of the land between the Jordan River and Mediterranean Sea; Israel controls 92% ; Netanyahu campaigns on never allowing a Palestinian state, while far-right Cabinet members suggest driving Palestinians out of Gaza

item.title: Google Maps Switches to "Lake America" as Canada Compares Change to SNL Skit
item.description: As Google Maps implements the "Lake America" name change following Trump's executive order, MapQuest refuses and surges in popularity while Canada's Ontario Premier Doug Ford calls the change "completely absurd." — Key takeaways: Google Maps now shows "Lake America" on mobile and desktop for US users, while Apple Maps initially kept "Lake Ontario" ; MapQuest publicly refused the name change and its tweet went viral, boosting the app to #1 on the US App Store ; "Lake America" appeared on Ontario government agency websites pulling data from Google Maps, despite Google saying Canadian users would see "Lake Ontario" ; Ontario Premier Doug Ford compared the change to a "Saturday Night Live" skit and installed a "Lake Ontario, today and forever" sign ; Google's region-localization means developers embedding Maps can set a Canada region to display "Lake Ontario"

item.title: 3 Hidden Google Maps Settings You Should Turn Off Right Away
item.description: Android Police identifies three Google Maps settings — background location tracking, automatic offline map downloads over cellular, and personalized ads based on visual search — that users should disable for privacy, battery life, and data conservation. — Key takeaways: Background location/Timeline tracking logs every location visited, duration, and route, and is enabled by default ; Automatic offline map downloads over cellular data drain battery, fill storage, and consume mobile data unnecessarily ; Google Maps serves personalized ads based on location, search history, and visual searches, pulling data from YouTube and Search ; Timeline tracking can be set to auto-delete after 3 months as a compromise ; Offline map downloads should be restricted to Wi-Fi only via Settings > Offline Maps > gear icon

item.title: UN General Assembly Endorses New World Map Showing Africa's True Size
item.description: The UN General Assembly endorsed the Equal Earth projection by 164-1, encouraging governments and institutions worldwide to replace the Mercator map that has distorted Africa's size for over four centuries. — Key takeaways: 164 member states voted in favor, only the US voted against, and 6 countries abstained ; The resolution encourages replacing the Mercator projection with Equal Earth but does not ban Mercator or impose a replacement ; Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland, but Mercator makes them appear similar in size ; French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called the correction "an act of truth" ; Advocacy group Africa No Filter wants accurate maps in schools, textbooks, newsrooms, and digital platforms

item.title: Google Maps Bluetooth Beacons Bring Precise Navigation to Tunnels
item.description: Google Maps now uses Bluetooth beacons installed in tunnels to maintain navigation continuity when GPS signals drop, an Android-only feature that Waze has offered for years. — Key takeaways: Google Maps uses Bluetooth beacons installed in tunnels to maintain navigation when GPS signal is lost ; The feature is activated via Settings > Navigation > Driving options > "Tunnel Bluetooth beacon" ; Currently Android-only because Apple limits background Bluetooth usage on iPhone ; Waze has offered a similar beacon-based tunnel navigation service for several years ; The feature provides real-time positioning information inside tunnels where GPS is unavailable

item.title: Can You Guess the Real Size of Each Country on the New World Map?
item.description: Al Jazeera launched an interactive map quiz that lets users guess which country is bigger, then morphs the map from Mercator to Equal Earth to reveal how distortion has been shrinking Africa and other equatorial regions for centuries. — Key takeaways: The interactive quiz lets users pick which country is bigger, then morphs from Mercator to Equal Earth to show the true proportions ; On a Mercator map, Greenland appears roughly the size of Africa, which is actually 14 times larger ; The distortion inflates Europe, Russia, and North America while shrinking Africa, Latin America, and South Asia ; The US called the resolution a "radical ideological project" and voted alone against it ; Togo plans a meeting in Lomé early next year with UNESCO, the African Union, and tech companies including Google to discuss implementation

item.title: How the GNIS Lake Ontario/Lake America Name Change Will Appear in Google Maps
item.description: Google's official blog explains that Maps will show "Lake America" to US users, "Lake Ontario" to Canadian users, and both names to everyone else, following the GNIS name change under Trump's executive order. — Key takeaways: The US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) formally changed "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" in the United States ; Google Maps follows official government sources (GNIS for the US) for name changes ; US users see "Lake America," Canadian users see "Lake Ontario," and users outside both countries see both names ; The update follows Google's long-standing policy for bodies of water with country-specific names ; Changes were rolling out as of August 30, 2026

item.title: Apple Maps Now Shows Ads You Cannot Turn Off
item.description: Apple has begun showing permanent, non-removable ads in Apple Maps for users in the US and Canada, with no opt-out setting — even for paying Apple One subscribers. — Key takeaways: Apple Maps now displays permanent ads on the main search screen and in search results for US and Canadian users ; There is no setting to turn off the ads, and even Apple One subscribers will see them ; Apple claims the ads are privacy-preserving, using on-device data not shared with advertisers ; The ads follow Apple's existing ad model in App Store, Apple News, and Apple TV ; Apple plans to expand the ads to the rest of North America soon

item.title: Why the UN's New World Map Won't Change Google Maps Anytime Soon
item.description: The UN's adoption of the Equal Earth projection resolution won't change Google Maps because the app's tiling system depends on Mercator's angle-preserving properties, and the resolution is nonbinding. — Key takeaways: The UN resolution passed with 164 votes in favour, 1 against (US), and 6 abstentions, but is nonbinding ; France announced it will switch official maps from Mercator to Eckert IV projection ; Google Maps uses a square-tile system since 2005 that requires Mercator's angle-preserving properties at all zoom levels ; Equal Earth and Eckert IV preserve surface areas but sacrifice angular accuracy, making them incompatible with current tile-based mapping infrastructure ; Togo plans to meet with Google, the African Union, and UNESCO within six months to discuss practical implementation

item.title: GIS Maps to Be Attached to Sale Deeds from October in Maharashtra
item.description: Maharashtra will attach GIS maps to property sale deeds starting October 2026, replacing decades-old boundary descriptions with precise digital maps in an initial 10-district rollout. — Key takeaways: GIS-linked sale deeds will replace textual boundary descriptions in Maharashtra ; Initial rollout covers 10 districts, with statewide expansion to follow ; The system integrates land records, building footprints, and satellite imagery ; The 'mojini' (land measurement) system will be implemented before registration ; Benefits include precise identification, fewer boundary disputes, and fraud deterrence

item.title: What Different World Maps Get Right — and What They Get Wrong
item.description: The BBC provides a comparative analysis of the world's most prominent map projections — Mercator, Equal Earth, and Peters — explaining the trade-offs between area accuracy, shape fidelity, and navigational utility. — Key takeaways: No flat map can perfectly represent a spherical Earth; every projection sacrifices something ; Mercator preserves compass bearings but massively distorts area, making Africa look Greenland-sized ; Equal Earth, adopted by the UN, preserves area accuracy but cannot be used for navigation ; The Peters projection (1973) also preserves area but severely distorts shapes of landmasses ; Critics argue Mercator's distortions have psychological effects, shaping how regions are perceived politically and economically

item.title: UN Tells the World: Stop Making Africa Look Small
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted overwhelmingly to adopt the "Correct the Map" resolution, urging governments, schools, and tech companies to stop using maps that make Africa look smaller than it is. — Key takeaways: The resolution passed with 164 votes in favour, 1 against (United States), and 6 abstentions ; The vote encourages governments, schools, and tech companies to adopt equal-area map projections ; Togo spearheaded the resolution on behalf of the African Union ; Togo announced it would change maps in schools starting this year ; The resolution is nonbinding but carries significant symbolic and practical weight

item.title: Kan TomTom Terugkeren Naar de Hoogtijdagen van de Jaren Nul?
item.description: BNR Nieuwsradio examines whether TomTom can return to its golden years by pivoting from failed consumer products to enterprise and government clients. — Key takeaways: TomTom has shifted focus from consumer products to enterprise and government clients ; The company has had a string of failed consumer product launches ; The B2B pivot raises questions about whether TomTom can match its peak performance ; The article examines TomTom's strategic transformation and market positioning ; TomTom's map data and location intelligence remain core assets

item.title: Waze contre Google Maps : 4 Points Forts de Waze
item.description: Despite Google owning Waze for over a decade, the community-driven navigation app still outperforms Google Maps in four key areas: real-time incident reporting, volunteer-managed local data, EV charging routing, and speed camera alerts. — Key takeaways: Waze's community-driven incident reporting remains superior to Google Maps ; Volunteer contributors update local data that algorithms cannot capture ; Waze offers EV-specific connector type and charging network preferences ; Google Maps excels at finding businesses, reviews, and offline resources ; The two platforms have not merged despite a decade of shared ownership

item.title: UN to Vote on Adopting New World Map That Shows Africa's True Scale
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted on a Togo-sponsored resolution to phase out the Mercator projection in favour of the Equal Earth map, which accurately depicts Africa's true size relative to other continents. — Key takeaways: Togo's foreign minister Robert Dussey sponsored the resolution on behalf of the African Union's 55 member states ; The Mercator projection, created in 1569, makes Africa appear similar in size to Greenland despite being 14 times larger ; The campaign promotes the 2018 Equal Earth projection as a more accurate alternative ; Critics call the Mercator distortion "cartographic colonialism" for visually diminishing the global south ; The resolution is nonbinding but could influence classroom curricula and technology platforms
